name: SteelSeries Arctis Nova Pro Wireless
wired: Via base station: 3.5mm line-in/out, USB, optical in
spatial: On-device virtual 7.1 · 360° Spatial Audio · full Sonar suite on PC (parametric EQ, AI mic)
soft: SteelSeries GG + Sonar (Windows only for Sonar)
micNote: ClearCast Gen 2, marketed as broadcast-grade. One of the best retractable mics; Sonar adds AI noise removal and a parametric mic EQ on PC.
battery: 2× 22 h hot-swap batteries, infinite via swap
best: Best all-rounder + the base station's optical in is the single most useful port for a living-room TV/Jellyfin feed.
extra: Base station switches 2 sources (e.g. PC + PS5) with a dial. ANC is competent, not class-leading. Also sold as Nova Pro Wireless X (Xbox).

name: SteelSeries Arctis Nova Pro Omni
w24: Base station + dongle, all platforms incl. Xbox
spatial: Most configurable spatial software on the market (Sonar) + on-device 7.1
micNote: Same ClearCast Gen 2 as the Nova Pro Wireless, with the widest set of Sonar mic-processing options.
best: The Nova Pro for people who also want the Xbox path and the deepest EQ/spatial tuning.
extra: 2026 flagship variant. Premium price; functionally the Nova Pro Wireless with wider platform support and expanded Sonar.

name: SteelSeries Arctis Nova 7 Gen 2
spatial: 360° Spatial Audio · Sonar virtual surround on PC
micNote: ClearCast Gen 2 again — clear and usable for chat/calls, a touch thinner and less full than the Nova Pro. Sonar processing helps on PC.
best: Cheapest headset that truly mixes BT + 2.4 GHz at once. Great value.
extra: No ANC, no base station. Xbox variant exists. Widely recommended mid-tier pick for 2026.

name: Audeze Maxwell
spatial: Dolby Atmos for Headphones built in on the Xbox model; on PC/PS works with OS/Sonar spatial. Audeze HRTF processing.
micNote: Broadcast-grade detachable boom, widely rated the best headset mic you can buy; also has a usable internal mic for Bluetooth calls. Audeze HQ adds full mic EQ + noise gate.
best: Best raw sound quality in the class — planar drivers. Sounds great with no software at all.
extra: Heavy (~490 g / clamp-y). PS5 model ($299) vs Xbox model ($329, includes the Dolby licence). No ANC.

name: Corsair Virtuoso Max Wireless
micNote: Omnidirectional broadcast-grade capsule; a long-standing streaming/content-creation favourite. iCUE adds noise gate, sidetone and mic EQ.
best: Atmos + good ANC + simultaneous dual-wireless without a base station.
extra: iCUE is a heavy install. PC and Xbox versions. Metal build, memory-foam pads.

name: Razer BlackShark V3 Pro
micNote: HyperClear Super Wideband — wide frequency range, rated the best mic for competitive voice comms. Synapse adds a mic EQ and noise-gate.
best: Competitive-FPS positional accuracy; well-reviewed for movie immersion too.
extra: BT and 2.4 GHz switch, don't mix. Synapse is bloated. Tuning roller on the cup.

name: Razer Barracuda Pro
soft: Razer Synapse / Audio app (Windows, mobile app for EQ)
micNote: Dual beamforming slots in the cup — no boom. Kills keyboard/background noise very well, but your voice sounds faint and a bit muffled in recordings. Fine for calls, weak for streaming.
best: Doubles as a street/travel ANC headphone — no boom mic, cleaner look.
extra: 2022 model, still current. Switch not mix. Bluetooth EQ via mobile app.

name: Logitech G Pro X 2 Lightspeed
micNote: Raw capture is average; Blue VO!CE processing in G HUB (EQ, de-esser, noise reduction, compressor) lifts it to genuinely good — but that is Windows-only.
best: Neutral tuning, light, sounds fine unplugged; esports staple.
extra: No ANC. G HUB needed only for EQ / DTS toggle. Triple connectivity (dongle, BT, wired).

name: Logitech G733 Lightspeed
micNote: Thin and a little boxy. Fine for party/Discord chat, not for streaming or recording. Non-detachable, so it is always sticking out.
best: Cheap, light, colourful. Pure PC/PS 2.4 GHz headset.
extra: No Bluetooth at all. Thin bass. Popular budget pick.

name: Logitech G Astro A50 X
w24: Base station (all links route through it) + 2.4 GHz
wired: Base station: HDMI 2.1 in/out ×3 (PS5+Xbox+PC), optical in, USB
spatial: Dolby Atmos (licence included, auto on Win/Xbox) + DTS Headphone:X
micNote: Clear, solid broadcast-ish quality — flip up to mute. Not detachable, and not quite at Corsair/Audeze level, but well above the budget crowd.
best: One base station switches video + audio across three consoles (PLAYSYNC). Optical in works for a TV feed.
extra: Most expensive mainstream headset. No ANC. Everything depends on the base station — not portable. Astro A50 Gen 5 (2025, ~$300) is the cheaper no-HDMI sibling, also with optical in.

name: Sony INZONE H9 II
spatial: Sony 360 Spatial Sound for Gaming — personalised HRTF from an ear photo (PC + PS5)
soft: INZONE Hub (Windows) / mobile app for the ear-photo profile
micNote: Improved over the first H9 — clear and clean for chat and calls. Some reviewers still want a bit more body/warmth. AI noise reduction in INZONE Hub.
best: Best-in-class personalised spatial if you're on PS5 + PC; lighter than the first H9.
extra: 360 profile is tied to Sony's ecosystem. Good ANC. H7 II / H5 are cheaper (H5 ~$149, no ANC).

name: Sony INZONE H5
micNote: Bright and intelligible for chat. Retracts into the cup when not in use. Similar character to the H9 II, slightly less refined.
best: Cheapest way into Sony's 360 spatial for PC/PS5.
extra: No ANC. Lightweight. BT switches, doesn't mix.

name: Sony PlayStation Pulse Elite
w24: PlayStation Link USB adapter (proprietary lossless 2.4 GHz)
bt: BT only via a separate PS Link adapter / limited on-headset BT
spatial: Tempest 3D AudioTech (PS5 hardware) — one of the two most reliable spatial implementations
soft: None — EQ lives in the PS5 system UI; no PC app
micNote: AI-enhanced noise rejection is the real strength — background noise vanishes. Voice itself is usable but not the crispest; reviews split between 'surprisingly clear' and 'a little muffled'. No PC mic software.
best: Cheapest planar-magnetic wireless headset, and Tempest 3D is excellent for PS5 games/movies.
extra: Really a PS5 accessory. PS Link also works on PC/Mac but you lose Tempest (that's PS5-only). No true multipoint.

name: HyperX Cloud III Wireless
micNote: HyperX house mic — reliably clear and intelligible, a little compressed/thin vs the broadcast-grade options. Consistently praised as good for the price.
best: Marathon battery, comfortable, cheap, sounds good with zero software.
extra: No Bluetooth — deal-breaker if you want phone audio in the same cups. PC/PS 2.4 GHz only.

name: HyperX Cloud Alpha Wireless
micNote: Same HyperX character as the Cloud III — clear, slightly compressed, well above budget headsets. No onboard DSP tricks.
best: You charge it three times a year. Warm, pleasant tuning.
extra: No BT, no ANC, no wired mode. Pure 2.4 GHz workhorse.

name: Turtle Beach Stealth Pro II
w24: USB dongle + base station / charging dock
spatial: Dolby Atmos + Turtle Beach Superhuman Hearing · Waves 3D
micNote: Clear with a slightly dark/warm tone. Swarm II adds mic monitoring and noise gate. Solid, not standout.
best: Hot-swap batteries and a dock like the Nova Pro, plus a portable dongle the A50 X lacks.
extra: Superhuman Hearing (footstep boost) is polarising. Multi-platform variants (PS/Xbox). No optical in on the dock.

name: Turtle Beach Stealth 700 Gen 3
spatial: Dolby Atmos / Windows Sonic · Superhuman Hearing
micNote: Integrated flip-down boom — fine for chat, muffled and boxy for streaming/recording. Non-detachable.
best: Mid-price ANC headset that genuinely mixes game + phone audio.
extra: Platform-specific SKUs. No wired fallback. Good value for the feature set.

name: EPOS H3Pro Hybrid
micNote: Sennheiser/EPOS voice pedigree — natural, full and detailed, among the best headset mics ever shipped. Lift the boom to mute; detach it entirely for a clean look.
best: Discontinued but often under $100 — Sennheiser-lineage sound, ANC, BT mixing at a bargain.
extra: Stock is drying up. Gaming Suite optional. Great clearance buy if you find one.
